evals.prompt: Open https://example.com in the browser and start a local screencast so I can watch it.
evals.expected_output: The page is opened, the relay is started through the bundled script, the browser is nudged to emit a frame, and the user gets the localhost viewer URL.
assertions: The workflow opens the requested page with agent-browser
The relay is started with bash scripts/start-relay.sh
The workflow reloads or otherwise changes the page so Chrome sends the first frame
The final response includes http://localhost:3456 or the configured local viewer URL

evals.prompt: Screencast my local file-based prototype and watch ./demo for changes so viewers see reloads automatically.
evals.expected_output: The relay starts with WATCH set to the requested directory and the response explains the local viewer URL.
assertions: The start command uses the WATCH environment variable
The relay is started via the bundled start script
The response does not expose the relay publicly unless explicitly asked

evals.prompt: Start the screencast and give me a public URL using Tailscale Funnel.
evals.expected_output: The local screencast is started first, then a public sharing command is provided or run only because the user explicitly asked for it.
assertions: The local relay is started before public sharing is addressed
The response uses an explicitly requested public-sharing mechanism rather than assuming one
The answer still includes the local viewer URL as the primary relay endpoint
